SB01-q01-7im91a: 12 feet is the most dangerous part in front, and the side and rear distance; the front zone reaches 30 feet.
50 feet is part of the blind spot behind the bus; the front danger zone reaches 30 feet.
SB01-q02-skthob: The zone does reach 30 feet, but the first 12 feet from the bumper is the most dangerous part.
The handbook names the first 12 feet in front of the bumper as the most dangerous area.
SB01-q03-dwjqok: 10 feet is how far students walk from the bus after unloading; the side and rear zones are 12 feet.
30 feet is the front danger zone limit; the sides and rear reach 12 feet.
SB01-q04-lgwpj2: Students use the right side, but the left side is the one always dangerous because of passing cars.
Behind the bus is a danger zone, but passing cars make the left side always dangerous.
SB01-q05-sw7hiq: 100 feet is too short; flat mirrors should show 200 feet, or 4 bus lengths, behind the bus.
400 feet is how far the blind spot behind the bus can reach, not the flat mirror view.
SB01-q06-7nk1cb: 12 feet is the rear danger zone, not the blind spot behind the bus.
200 feet is what flat mirrors should show; the blind spot runs 50 to 150 feet, up to 400.
SB01-q07-nwdv2e: Above the windshield on the driver's side is where the overhead inside mirror goes.
Convex mirrors are mounted below the outside flat mirrors, not on the rear door.
SB01-q08-tm3g4h: Convex mirrors should show the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
Convex mirrors should show the front of the rear tires touching the ground.
SB01-q09-iamcv8: Watching students inside is the overhead inside mirror's job.
Crossview mirrors show the area in front of the bumper, not traffic far behind the bus.
SB01-q10-g4104u: The California rule in this section (CCR Title 13 §1258) is about a front crossview mirror, not strobe lights.
A glass-bottom rear door is only mentioned as something some buses have; the required item is a crossview mirror.
SB01-q11-onq36t: 200 feet behind the bus is the flat mirror view; the overhead mirror is for students inside.
Front tires are what the crossview mirrors show; the overhead mirror shows the rear window and all students.
SB01-q12-6mml18: 100 feet is at the short end of the turn signal range; amber lights go on at least 200 feet out.
Amber lights warn before the stop; the red lights are the ones used once you are stopped.
SB01-q13-w2lpf6: 500 feet is not the rule; turn on the right signal about 100–300 feet, or 3–5 seconds, before.
The signal goes on before you pull over, about 100–300 feet or 3–5 seconds ahead.
SB01-q14-c2h6uj: Stopping right next to them is wrong; stop at least 10 feet away so they walk to the bus in view.
30 feet is the front danger zone limit; the stopping rule is at least 10 feet from the students.
SB01-q15-lzp9un: At every stop, put it in Park (or Neutral) and set the parking brake, not just hold the service brake.
Holding the service brake is not enough; set the parking brake at every stop.
SB01-q16-v8f6bg: The amber lights go on while you slow down; the red lights go on when traffic is a safe distance away.
Red lights go on before students board, once traffic is a safe distance away with the stop arm out.
SB01-q17-kad2x7: Asking the others is only the first step; never leave until you secure the bus and check around and under it.
Waiting is not the rule; secure the bus, take the key, and check around and under the bus.
SB01-q18-41e4yr: Behind the bus is a danger zone; students walk at least 10 feet from the side, where you can see them.
Walking along the side keeps them in the danger zone; they must move at least 10 feet away.
SB01-q19-ow8o34: Too narrow: prekindergarten, kindergarten, and grades 1 through 8 must be escorted.
The rule covers prekindergarten, kindergarten, and grades 1 through 8, not every student.
SB01-q20-30z9qm: Students must never cross behind the bus; every crossing student walks in front of it.
Students cross in front of the bus, and the bus waits until they are safely across.
SB01-q21-9rbn53: Never back up after missing a stop, even with hazard lights on; follow local procedures.
Letting the student walk back in the lane is not the rule; do not back up and follow local procedures.
SB01-q22-bwwphr: The walk-through looks for hiding or sleeping students and items left behind, not seat belts.
Testing the stop arm is not the reason; the walk-through looks for hiding or sleeping students and left items.
SB01-q23-tr2o7t: A child picking up a dropped object can vanish from the driver's view; leave it and get the driver's attention.
Never go under the bus; move out of the danger zone and get the driver's attention.
SB01-q24-h80nxh: The named age group is at least 8 but under 16, not under 8.
The named age group is at least 8 but under 16, not 16 and older.
